summary.tldr: Excludes most natural health products from the Food and Drugs Act's therapeutic product definition, except nicotine replacement therapy products, and keeps some recall and penalty rules in place.
what_it_does: Redefines “therapeutic product” to mean a drug, a device, a mix of drugs and devices, or a natural health product that contains nicotine or its salts and is used in nicotine replacement therapy.
Adds a rule saying certain Food and Drugs Act monitoring and enforcement sections still apply to natural health products, despite the new definition.
Adds regulation-making power for natural health product recalls and for penalties when certain natural health product rules are broken.
Repeals section 21.321 and subsection 21.8(2) of the Food and Drugs Act.

Bars new or continuing prosecutions for offences under sections 31.2 or 31.4 involving natural health products, if they happened after section 500 of the Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1 came into force and before this Act takes effect.
summary.background: The bill changes the Food and Drugs Act's definition of therapeutic product. It keeps nicotine replacement therapy products in that definition, but removes most other natural health products.
